message.content:
**The three most widely‑recognized “great” schisms in Christian history are:**

| # | Schism | Year | Key Parties | Main Cause(s) |
|---|--------|------|-------------|---------------|
| 1 | **East–West Schism** (also called the *Great Schism* of 1054) | 1054 CE | Roman Catholic Church (West) ↔ Eastern Orthodox Church (East) | Long‑standing theological, liturgical, and political differences—most notably the *Filioque* clause, papal primacy, and cultural‑linguistic divides. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE (often dated to 1517 with Martin Luther’s 95 Theses) | Roman Catholic Church ↔ various Protestant movements (Lutheranism, Calvinism, Anglicanism, etc.) | Doctrinal disputes over indulgences, papal authority, Scripture vs. tradition, and the nature of salvation. |
| 3 | **Old Catholic Schism** | 1870 CE (following the First Vatican Council) | Roman Catholic Church ↔ Old Catholic Churches (e.g., Union of Utrecht) | Opposition to the declaration of papal infallibility, desire for national churches to govern themselves, and resistance to certain doctrinal developments. |

> **Why these three?**  
> • They each split a major, historically unified Christian body into distinct, enduring traditions.  
> • Each had profound theological, ecclesiological, and cultural consequences that shaped the course of Western and Eastern Christianity.  
> • Their legacies continue to influence inter‑church dialogue, ecumenical efforts, and the internal life of the churches involved.

---

### Quick Summary

| Schism | Year | Main Parties | Core Issue |
|--------|------|--------------|------------|
| East–West | 1054 | Catholic vs. Orthodox | Papal primacy & Filioque |
| Protestant | 1517–1648 | Catholic vs. Protestants | Indulgences, authority, Scripture |
| Old Catholic | 1870 | Catholic vs. Old Catholics | Papal infallibility & national autonomy |

These three events are often referred to as the “great” schisms because they represent the most significant, lasting splits in Christian history.
